full_judgment:
Chowdhury A.T.M. Masud, J.—This Reference to the full Bench arises out of an appeal from the original judgment and decree, of the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Comilla, in a suit lied by the respondent here, praying for several declarations, including a declaration that the order of is dismissal from service dated 6.12.63 is null and void and not binding upon him. 

 5. The trial Court has decreed the suit relying upon a Division Bench decision of, the Dacca High Court reported as M. Noman Vs. Dacca Improvement Trust and others in 16 DLR (Dacca) 536, holding that in view of the admitted position that no rules have been framed under Articles 47 of the Basic Democracies Order, 1959, in respect of holding enquiries, against servants of the local councils, the proceeding drawn up against the plaintiff was without authority and the order of dismissal and other orders passed in the said proceeding were null and void and not binding against the plaintiff. 

 6. The defendant, District Council of Comilla preferred an appeal being F.A. No. 503 of 1968 against the said decree, passed by the learned Subordinate Judge. In course of hearing of the said appeal by a Division Bench of this Court, it was contended on behalf of the appellant, that the aforesaid Noman's case was not correctly decided. The Division Bench after hearing the learned Advocate of the parties and considering certain decisions cited before them, was of opinion that Noman's case was not correctly decided, Hence this Reference to the Full Bench on the following questions: 

 7. He has also placed before us the relevant provisions of the Basic Democracies Order, 1959. He has submitted that the plaintiff was an employee of a Real council and that under Clause 4(b) of article 45 of the said order, the District Council was competent to suspend, remove, dismiss or otherwise punish any person appointed under Clause (2) of the said article. He further submits that although actions mentioned above can be taken against an employee, subject to the provisions of this Order and the Rules, but since the local council was not empowered to frame any rule, framing of the rule being the function of the Government, failure of the Government to frame any rule would not make the local council incompetent to take disciplinary action against its employee, for which them is specific provision in the Basic Democracies Order. He submits that the Noman's case. where a different view has been taken and on the basis of which the suit has been decreed, has not been correctly decided.
